doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Union calls, concerts and Cherokee in twelve keys in Harlem
summary: Finding gigs through the union, concerts at Town Hall, and Saturday jam sessions in Harlem.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: this place. But I had a quartet and I was playing clarinet and tenor I guess, and probably a little flute but I remember clarinet and tenor. And we had a six night a week gig. I don’t remember years too well.
Did you have to go down to the union and like hang out waiting for gigs or were those days gone?

Yeah that was the days when you went down to the union and said do you have Saturday? You know, I mean anything happening on Saturday? Or you’d see people that says hey you working Saturday? We got a gig for you. You know, this wedding, this bar mitzvah, this party. So there was a little coming in that way. I was doing some concerts around New York too. I haven’t thought about this for a long time, but I did some, this is just fragments of association. I did one concert with, I had a small group at Town Hall, I think I had Charlie Persip and I forgot who else. Well I don’t remember too well. But another concert in Connecticut, and who was sitting in the audience right in front of us but Dizzy Gillespie and Sonny Stitt so I was a little nervous doing those jazz concerts. So I got to do some of those and the recordings and jamming. I remember going to Harlem and I guess every Saturday I’d jam with a piano player and bass player. We’d go through the twelve keys on “Cherokee.”
It’s like a little testing ground, ey?

Yes, we’d play “Cherokee” in twelve keys, and other tunes in twelve keys, like all working out together. That was good you know. And that was the days when you could get to go to Harlem and it was like everybody’s welcome.
